title: PPA Price Escalator Dispute — Ambiguous CPI Index Reference
question: What is Conduit's strongest legal position for the Year 4 price escalator dispute with High Plains Wind LLC?

contributor.name: Sarah Lindqvist
contributor.title: Renewable Energy PPA Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Power purchase agreements, price escalator mechanisms, contract interpretation, regulatory cost recovery

choices: Conduit should apply CPI-U national (2.8%) based on two years of established course of dealing accepted without objection by both parties, supported by SAP payment records confirming prior pricing
Conduit should apply the 2.0% floor since it avoids the CPI ambiguity entirely; the price should be $25.46 x 1.02 = $25.97/MWh
Conduit should reject the invoice and halt payment until legal provides formal guidance, as the contract is too ambiguous to determine the correct price without an amendment
Conduit must accept CPI-W Denver metro (4.1%) because the contract is ambiguous and the developer's interpretation is reasonable; the price should be $26.50/MWh
